content.text: You are working on Resurgo's web app on the `web` branch in this worktree. Read web/NOTES.md, docs/ANIMATION.md, api/main.py, web/src/components/Logo.tsx and web/src/pages/Landing.tsx first. Commit in small steps. ## 1. Logos: original artwork, large and very visible The owner says the logos are too small and must be the original logo images. New original files are in `web/public/logos/` (uncommitted). `web/public/logos/SOURCES.md` says where each came from and exactly how each one is drawn. Commit them. - **"Built with" row.** Replace the hero sentence "Built on neatlogs tracing and Entire checkpoints" with a row headed "BUILT WITH", in the same label style as "WORKS WITH". - **neatlogs:** the app icon (`neatlogs-icon.png`, 40px) beside the wordmark (`neatlogs-wordmark.webp` as a mask, about 26px tall). Colour the wordmark #F5F5F2 in dark and ink in light. - **Entire:** the full logo (`entire.svg` as a mask, about 32px tall). Colour it #1C1917 in light and #FFFFFF in dark. These are Entire's own colours. - Under each logo, a small caption: "traces every run" and "checkpoints every commit". - Leave cfo.ai out until the plan exists. - **"Works with" row.** Use the original full-colour files at 44px tall, drawn as plain `` with their own colours (not masks): `node-js-icon.svg`, `pnpm-frame.svg`, `npm-square.svg`, `yarn-kitten-circle.svg`, `foundry-logo.png`, `rust-logo-blk.svg` (inverted to white in dark mode, as Checkly does for black logos), `docker-mark-blue.svg`, and the GitHub mark as a mask (#1F2328 in light, #FFFFFF in dark). Gap of about 28px. Show the name under each logo in small muted text, so the row reads at a glance. - Delete the old single-colour files the page no longer uses: `node.svg`, `pnpm.svg`, `npm.svg`, `yarn.svg`, `docker.svg`, `rust.svg`, `foundry-mark.png`. Keep `github.svg`, `bun.svg`, `cfo.svg`, `entire.svg` and the neatlogs files. - Keep accessible names: `alt`, or `role="img"` with `aria-label`, on every logo. Keep `title` tooltips. - At 420px both rows wrap cleanly, with no sideways scroll. ## 2. The GitHub App callback (it is a 404 today) After someone installs the "Resurgo Agent" App, GitHub sends them to `/auth/github/callback?code=…&installation_id=…&setup_action=install`. Build the receiving end. Checks themselves are run by a separate worker on the host. It isn't in this repo yet and gets built next, so stick exactly to the file contract below. - **Queue directory.** Read `QUEUE_DIR` from the environment; the container mounts it at `/queue`. The API writes requests into `$QUEUE_DIR/requests/` and only reads `$QUEUE_DIR/status/`. - **`GET /auth/github/callback`** (FastAPI, ahead of the SPA fallback): - Accept only an `installation_id` of 1 to 12 digits. Ignore `code` entirely; it is never stored or logged. - Write `$QUEUE_DIR/requests/.json` containing `{"installation_id": , "received": "", "setup_action": ""}`. Write it atomically (temp file, then rename). If the file already exists, leave it alone. - If `requests/` already holds 50 or more files, don't write. Redirect anyway, and let the page say the queue is full. - Redirect (303) to `/installed/`. On a bad or missing id, redirect to `/`. - **`GET /api/installations/{installation_id}`** returns `$QUEUE_DIR/status/.json` if it exists. Otherwise it returns `{"installation_id": id, "state": "received"}` when a request file exists, and 404 when neither exists. The status file, written by the worker, looks like this: ```json {"installation_id": 170024627, "account": "Timidan", "updated": "", "state": "received|checking|done|rejected", "reason": "", "repos": [{"repo": "owner/name", "sha": "<12 chars>", "path": "", "state": "queued|checking|done|skipped", "reason": "", "run_id": "", "result": "", "needs_approval": false, "pr": {"url": "...", "number": 1} }]} ``` - **Page `/installed/:id`** (React, in the site's style): - Headline: "Resurgo Agent is installed." - Then one plain line, true to the contract: Resurgo checks each repository you picked in a fresh container, one at a time, and opens a pull request only for a fix that passed in a clean container. Code changes wait for your approval. - Then the live list from `/api/installations/:id`, polled every 5 seconds until the state is `done` or `rejected`. Each repo shows its state, its result badge (reuse the gallery's status styles, including "Fix verified · awaiting approval"), a link to `/runs/` when there is one, and the PR link when there is one. - "received" with no list yet reads "Waiting for the runner to pick this up." "rejected" shows the reason. - Any motion follows docs/ANIMATION.md. - **Compose and Dockerfile.** - In `deploy/compose.yaml`, mount `${RESURGO_QUEUE_DIR}` at `/queue` read-write and set `QUEUE_DIR=/queue`. - Run the container as `user: "1000:1000"`, the host account that owns the queue, so the worker can read and remove what the API writes. The image must still work under that user. - **Tests.** One small API test, using FastAPI's TestClient and a temp QUEUE_DIR, that a good callback writes the request file and redirects, and that a bad id writes nothing. Run it with `uv run --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q api`, or however the repo runs its tests. ## 3. Check your work Run `npm run build` and `web/check-render.mjs` (420 and 1280px, light and dark) against the API already running on port 8787. Take close-up screenshots of both logo rows in both themes, plus the `/installed/` page for "received" and for a sample status (point a temporary QUEUE_DIR at a fake status file). Look at them yourself: are the logos large, crisp, in their original colours and clearly visible in both themes? Rules: - Don't push, don't merge, and don't edit hackathon.md. - Never read `.env` or `.entire/settings.local.json`. - Run no `docker` commands. - Never print secrets. - No tool or AI attribution in commits. - Finish with a short report: what changed, the check results with screenshot paths, and anything you weren't sure about.

42	def _load(run_dir: Path) -> dict | None:
43	    """result.json for a run, re-read only when the file changes."""
44	    path = run_dir / "result.json"
45	    try:

64	def _verified(result: dict) -> bool:
65	    """A run is verified when the separate clean container ran steps and it passed (flag, or every step exit 0)."""

71	def _status(result: dict) -> str:
72	    # runs | runs_with_gaps | broken are current. fixed | fail come from earlier agent versions,
73	    # which did write the verifier's steps: judge those by the steps, not by the old word.
74	    raw = str(result.get("result") or "unknown")

245	_HOW = """## How a run is proved
246	
247	1. **Fresh clone.** The agent container clones the repository at a pinned commit, picks the package manager from the lockfile, and runs install, build, test and start in order, stopping at the first failure.
248	2. **Diagnose.** Deterministic rules run first. A model is called only when a step failed; it proposes the least invasive fix (configuration before source code).
249	3. **Repair.** The fix is applied as a patch and the failed step is run again. Source-code changes are proposed and marked `needs_approval`; they are not applied on their own.
250	4. **Prove.** A second, separate container rebuilds from a fresh clone with the recipe and the patch only. Its steps are recorded as `verifier.steps`. The agent that wrote the fix cannot write to it.
251	
252	## Status vocabulary
253	
254	- `runs` (✓ Runs): the verifier ran and every step passed.
255	- `runs_with_gaps` (◐ Runs with gaps): the verifier passed, and the record lists `gaps` (things it could not exercise, such as a missing test script).
256	- `fix_awaiting_approval` (◆ Fix verified · awaiting approval): the fix passed in the clean container and changes source code, so it waits for the owner's approval. The repository itself does not run clean yet; `verified` is true because the verifier passed.
257	- `broken` (✗ Broken): a step failed and no verified fix exists.
258	- `checking` (◌ Checking): the run has started and has no record yet.
259	- `fixed` (◐ Fixed, unverified): only in records from an earlier agent version that have no verifier steps at all.
260	
261	A run counts as verified only when `verified` is true: the verifier has at least one step and all steps exited 0. Nothing is claimed beyond the recorded steps; for example a verifier that only ran `install` has proved the install, not the build.
262	"""
263	
264	_API = """## API (read-only, JSON)
265	
266	- `GET /api/runs`: every run, newest first. Each item carries `id`, `repo`, `sha`, `path`, `type`, `status`, `verified`, `duration_s`, `model_calls`, `fix_kind` (`config`, `code` or null), `needs_approval`, `gaps`, `agent_steps` and `verifier_steps` (`name`, `ok`, `duration_s`), `attempts` (`kind`, `files`, `result`, `status`, `confidence`, `rationale`), `error_line`, `problems`, `patch_preview`.
267	- `GET /api/runs/{id}`: one run as `{summary, result, fix_patch}`. `result` is the full record: steps with commands, exit codes, durations and output tails, model calls, and attempts. `fix_patch` is a unified diff or null.
268	- Run ids look like `20261010T120139Z-5c3370f` (UTC start time, then the short commit).
269	
270	## Pages
271	
272	- `/`: the landing page. `/runs`: the gallery. `/runs/{id}`: one run with a replay and its fix diff.
273	- `/index.md` and `/llms.txt`: this description.
274	"""
275

278	    head = (
279	        "# Resurgo\n\n"
280	        "> Resurgo fresh-clones a repository, repairs what rotted, and proves the fix in a separate clean container.\n\n"
281	        "Current state: a hackathon build. The GitHub App \"Resurgo Agent\" is installed on the repositories you pick. "
282	        "It opens a pull request only for a fix that passed in a clean container, and a change to source code waits "
283	        "for your approval. The runs below are recorded runs on public repositories. "
284	        "There are no customers, testimonials or benchmark claims on this site.\n\n"
285	    )
286	    live = ""
287	    try:
288	        latest: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
289	        for r in _rows():
290	            if r["repo"] and r["status"] != "checking":
291	                latest.setdefault((r["repo"], r["path"]), r)
292	        if latest:
293	            live = "## Latest run per repository\n\n" + "\n".join(
294	                f"- [{r['repo']}{'/' + r['path'] if r['path'] else ''}](/runs/{r['id']}): "
295	                f"{_STATUS_WORD.get(r['status'], r['status'])}"
296	                f"{', verified' if r['verified'] and r['status'] != 'fix_awaiting_approval' else ''}"
297	                f"{', fix: ' + r['fix_kind'] if r['fix_kind'] else ''}"
298	                for r in latest.values()
299	            ) + "\n\n"
300	    except HTTPException:
301	        pass  # RUNS_DIR not configured: describe the system without a live list
302	    if short:
303	        return head + live + "## Links\n\n- [Full description](/index.md)\n- [Run list as JSON](/api/runs)\n"
304	    return head + live + _API + "\n" + _HOW

322	    candidate = (DIST_DIR / rest).resolve()
323	    if rest and candidate.is_file() and DIST_DIR in candidate.parents:
324	        return FileResponse(candidate)
325	    index = DIST_DIR / "index.html"
326	    if not index.is_file():
327	        raise HTTPException(404, "web app is not built")
328	    return FileResponse(index)
